entity.name: Mao Zedong
entity.description: Founder of the People's Republic of China. A peasant's son who led the Long March, defeated the Nationalists, and ruled the world's most populous nation for 27 years. His policies caused both industrial transformation and the deadliest famine in human history.

story.name: Mao Zedong
story.description: Born a peasant in Hunan, discovers Marxism as a library assistant in Beijing, survives the Long March, founds the CCP in Shanghai, and launches the Cultural Revolution. The architect of modern China and its greatest catastrophes.

moments.name: Mao Zedong Is Born to a Peasant Family in Rural Hunan
moments.subtitle: A farmer's son who refused an arranged marriage and devoured books on revolution
moments.description: On December 26, 1893, Mao Zedong was born near Shaoshan village in Hunan province, during the final decades of the Qing dynasty. His father, Mao Yichang, had risen from impoverished peasant to one of the wealthiest farmers in Shaoshan. Mao described his father as a stern disciplinarian. At age 13, Mao's father arranged his marriage to 17-year-old Luo Yixiu; Mao refused to recognize the marriage and became a lifelong opponent of arranged marriage. Luo died in 1910 at age 20. Reading voraciously on his father's farm, Mao developed early political awareness from texts arguing for representative democracy and translations of Western philosophers.

moments.name: Mao Discovers Marxism While Working as a Library Assistant in Beijing
moments.subtitle: Snubbed by students for his peasant accent, the future chairman finds his ideology in a reading room
moments.description: In 1918, Mao Zedong moved to Beijing where his mentor Yang Changji secured him a job as assistant to Li Dazhao, the librarian at Peking University and an early Chinese Communist. Paid a low wage and living in a cramped room with seven other Hunanese students, Mao was snubbed by university students due to his rural accent and lowly position. But it was here that Mao first encountered Marxism through Li Dazhao's articles on the Russian October Revolution. Mao joined Li's study group and, as he later recalled, 'developed rapidly toward Marxism' during the winter of 1919. The library assistant would go on to lead the largest communist revolution in history.

moments.name: Mao Cofounds the Chinese Communist Party in a Shanghai Townhouse
moments.subtitle: Thirteen delegates meet secretly to launch a party that will rule 1.4 billion people
moments.description: In July 1921, Mao Zedong was one of 13 delegates who attended the First Congress of the Chinese Communist Party, held secretly in a townhouse in the French Concession of Shanghai. The meeting, organized with help from Soviet Comintern agents, brought together Marxist study groups from across China. When police raided a nearby building, the delegates moved the final session to a boat on South Lake in Jiaxing. The CCP started with roughly 50 members. Over the next 28 years, under Mao's eventual leadership, the party would fight a civil war, survive the Long March, and seize control of the world's most populous country.
moments.address: 106 Rue Wantz, French Concession, Shanghai, China

moments.name: Mao Takes Command of the Communist Party During the Long March
moments.subtitle: A military disaster gives a sidelined politician control of the revolution
moments.description: In January 1935, during the Long March, Mao Zedong was elevated to leadership of the Chinese Communist Party at the Zunyi Conference in Guizhou province. The CCP had been forced to abandon its base in Jiangxi province in October 1934 after Nationalist forces encircled them. What followed was a grueling 6,000-mile retreat through some of China's most inhospitable terrain. Of the roughly 86,000 who started the march, only about 8,000 survived to reach the new base in Yan'an, Shaanxi. The Zunyi Conference marked the beginning of Mao's dominance over the CCP, a position he would hold for the next 41 years until his death.

moments.name: Mao Zedong Dies at 82 After Ruling China for 27 Years
moments.subtitle: The chairman's death triggers a power struggle that reverses his final revolution
moments.description: On September 9, 1976, Mao Zedong died in Beijing at the age of 82, ending 27 years of rule over the People's Republic of China. Mao had suffered from a motor neuron disease in his final years and had been largely incapacitated. His death triggered an immediate power struggle: within a month, the Gang of Four -- including Mao's wife Jiang Qing -- were arrested, ending the Cultural Revolution he had launched in 1966. Deng Xiaoping took power in 1978 and reversed many of Mao's policies, opening China to market reforms. Mao's embalmed body was placed in a mausoleum in Tiananmen Square, where it remains on public display.
